newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris prosecutors hold 10 Moslem militants.
newsitem.headline: Paris prosecutors hold 10 Moslem militants.

text.p: French prosecutors are holding 10 Moslem militants, some of them allegedly trained as guerrillas in Bosnia, on suspicion of links to a guerrilla support network, justice sources said on Monday.

The 10 are believed to have no connection, however, to the December 3 bombing of a Paris commuter train in which four people died, an attack that investigators believe was staged by Moslem fundamentalists angry over French backing for Algeria.

The 10, among 20 people rounded up last Thursday in police raids in Paris and northern France, are suspected of ties to a gang of Moslem activists who staged a series of spectacular robberies of security vans and supermarkets in and around the northern city of Lille.
Five suspected members of the gang were killed by French and Belgian police last March.
Investigators believe other gang members escaped with the help of a support network spanning France, Turkey, Canada and Belgium, the justice sources said.

The network, which provided gang members with false identity papers, was believed to be run by three individuals who fought in Bosnia in the early 1990s, the sources said. Some of the 10 in custody received training in Bosnia, they said.
In Thursday's raids, police seized guerrilla training materials including videocassettes made in Bosnia, they said.

Thursday's raid was the third police swoop on suspected Moslem guerrilla haunts since the December 3 train attack. The raids have yielded little evidence connected with that bombing, police sources said.
